A front/side/back show a broadly plausible upright stance, forward head and both feet at similar depth; joints foot.L Z=2.80 and foot.R Z=2.53 cm support that reading. This is substantially closer than B. But photo-render presents a noticeably oblique torso/head while source is nearly frontal (camera final yaw-like entry 20.715 degrees). Image-right hand hangs flat alongside thigh rather than clearly supporting the clutch. Finger flexion 12 degrees on L is a weak generic curl, not demonstrated contact; wrist.L remains zero. Source image-right wrist is partly occluded, so exact wrist angle/depth cannot be judged. Source shoe on image-right points outward; A has both feet more parallel. Skirt-hidden hip/knee positions remain unknown and are not used as truth. Nonblind report openly states clutch contact not solved and collision NOT_RUN. Honesty about these limits is not a separate failure; actual failure is remaining visible action mismatch/incomplete grip. Independently reconstructed saved state produces exactly the reviewed OBJ and camera projection, so these visible defects belong to the final model rather than a stale render.

measurements.json explicitly defines neutral-pose model paths/distances, not photographed-person measurements; height 170, bust 90, waist 72, hips 96 are prior targets. The source publishes 180.34 cm / 33-25-34.5 inches with its own generic-model caveat. These are different evidence classes, and exact target agreement (maximum error about 0.00004 cm) demonstrates only reported calibration. Real person accuracy remains UNKNOWN. Additional read-only Runtime evaluation reproduced neutral and posed OBJ within 5e-9 cm and the projected joints within 2.3e-13 px. Retained independent-neutral-check JSON gives about 0.00004045 cm target error. These corroborate calibrated model consistency, not true human dimensions. Minor classification discrepancy: measurements.json labels upperArmLength/forearmLength mesh_parameter while CSV writes all rows prior; fitted lengths round back to 29/23, so no real-person accuracy claim follows.
